_description: Per-metric weights for confidence scoring. Not wired into computeConfidence() yet — this is config scaffolding to build the metric-aware confidence formula on top of. Weight is a relative multiplier (not required to sum to 1); higher = more trusted when this metric is the base_metric of the top evidence segment.

cvr.notes: Baseline/reference metric. Ratio of two counts (orders/sessions), moderately stable at typical volumes.

orders.notes: Raw count-based delta; percent change can swing sharply at low baseline order counts.

sessions.notes: High-volume, generally noisy metric; a sessions delta alone is a weaker signal of a meaningful change.

atc_rate.notes: Ratio metric similar to cvr but typically lower volume per segment, so noisier at the same session count.

atc_sessions.notes: Raw count-based delta, similar volatility profile to orders.

product_id.notes: Discrete, business-meaningful segments; usually decision-relevant and comparatively stable.

utm_source.notes: Coarse-grained traffic source, generally low-cardinality and stable.

utm_campaign.notes: Higher cardinality than source/medium; individual campaigns can have low, spiky volume.

utm_content.notes: Higher cardinality, often low volume per value.

utm_term.notes: Long-tail, high-cardinality, frequently sparse per value; noisiest UTM dimension.

landing_page_path.notes: Can be high-cardinality depending on site structure; volume per page varies widely.

landing_page_type.notes: Lower cardinality than landing_page_path (grouped page types), more stable.

referrer_name.notes: Moderate cardinality; volume can be concentrated in a few referrers with a long tail.
